haiku-low.q1: The unfiltered reports.row_count decides. 10,000 or fewer: CSV returned directly in the 200 response. More than 10,000: a queued background job emails a 24-hour download link.
haiku-low.q2: The partial unique index rejects the insert. The API returns 200 with the existing queued or running export's id and status and queues nothing.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link expires after 24 hours. The stored file is removed by the bucket's lifecycle rule 7 days after creation.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, retries after 60 s then 300 s. After the last failure, the row is marked failed and the user is emailed report_export_failed; the page shows the failed label.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica, on both the small direct path and the large background path.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports table in the primary database. The page loads GET .../exports/latest and polls GET /api/exports/{id} every 5 seconds while queued or running.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000-row batches from the replica, encodes CSV into an 8 MB buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part. About 115 parts; memory holds one batch and one buffer.
haiku-low.q8: An exception aborts the multipart upload and re-raises. A crash or timeout leaves it uncompleted and invisible, discarded after 24 h. The next attempt restarts from the first row with a new upload.
haiku-low.q9: Stored as frozen filters and columns on the report_exports row. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job loads the row from the primary database.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The second concurrent insert violates it.
haiku-low.q11: The signed URL is created and the link email sent before status becomes succeeded. If the row is succeeded or failed, the job does nothing; if running with object_key set, it goes straight to the email step.
haiku-low.q12: If the replica fails before any bytes are sent, the API returns 503; mid-stream, it drops the connection. The page saves no file, shows the failed label, and nothing retries automatically.

sonnet.q1: The unfiltered reports.row_count decides. 10,000 rows or fewer: the CSV is returned directly in the response (200, text/csv), with no job or storage. More than 10,000: the API saves an export record, queues a background job and returns 202 at once. The job writes the file to the exports bucket and emails the user a download link valid for 24 hours.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) for status queued/running is violated, so the API returns 200 with the existing export's id and status. It queues nothing and creates no new row.
sonnet.q3: The link works for 24 hours. The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation. No cleanup job is needed.
sonnet.q4: Three attempts, with retries after 60 s then 300 s. After the last failure, on_final_failure sets the row to failed (with error and finished_at). The page shows "Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again." and the user can click again to start a new export. The user is emailed "report_export_failed", but that email may itself fail, in which case it is only logged.
sonnet.q5: The read replica, for both the small and the large path.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports row's status column in the primary database. The page polls GET /api/exports/{export_id} every 5 seconds while the status is queued or running. On page load it calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest to get the user's newest export of that report. The page keeps no export state of its own.
sonnet.q7: It streams the file in parts. It reads 5,000 rows at a time from the replica, encodes them as CSV into an in-memory buffer, and uploads a part each time the buffer reaches 8 MB. It then completes the multipart upload. Memory holds only one batch plus one 8 MB buffer. The 2M-row, ~900 MB report is about 115 parts. The document does not state anything about a 512 MB worker.
sonnet.q8: On an exception, the job calls abort_multipart and re-raises. If the worker crashes or times out, the upload is never completed, so nothing becomes visible and the bucket discards it after 24 h. The next attempt starts again at step 6 with a new upload from the first row, and nothing carries over. The exception is when the file was already completed and object_key saved: then the retry skips writing and goes straight to the email step.
sonnet.q9: They are stored on the report_exports row (filters and columns columns), frozen at creation. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job loads the row from the primary database to get them.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status in ('queued','running') in the primary database. The second insert violates it.
sonnet.q11: The file must be complete: complete_multipart has succeeded and object_key is saved on the row. If the row is succeeded or failed, the job returns and does nothing. If it is running with object_key set, it skips writing and only sends the email (step 8) and then marks the export succeeded.
sonnet.q12: If the replica fails before any bytes are sent, the API returns 503. If it fails mid-stream, the API drops the connection. Either way the page saves no file and shows "Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again." Nothing retries automatically, and no record or stored file exists.
